topics.title: Hard question
topics.text:
Compute the product $(4\div 3)(5\div 4)(6\div 5)(7\div 6)(8\div 7)(9\div 8)$.



Let's break this down.



= $(4\div 3)$

= $(a\div b)$

= $(a\div b)$ = 1 1/b



This works for any of these problems:



$(4\div 3)$ = 1  1/3

$(5\div 4)$ = 1  1/4

$(6\div 5)$ = 1  1/5

$(7\div 6)$ = 1  1/6

$(8\div 7)$ = 1  1/7

$(9\div 8)$ = 1  1/8



And 1 1/3 x 1 1/4 x 1 1/5 x 1 1/6 x 1 1/7 x 1 1/8 = 3.



So: $(4\div 3)(5\div 4)(6\div 5)(7\div 6)(8\div 7)(9\div 8)$ = 3.

topics.title: Fun Logic Puzzle
topics.text:
So my friend's brother asked us a question, and it was actually pretty funny. It seems very complicated at first, and unsolvable, but after a while, you should quickly see the answer. Not sure if this should be in another forum or not, but for now, I'll put it here.



Solve the following expression:



$\frac{(x-a)(x-b)(x-c)...(x-z)}{26!}$.



HintThe solution is an integer.




If you haven't solved it, don't give up yet! It's a logic puzzle, so you have to look at through a different way. If you just want to see the answer, here it is:



SolutionThere is a long and a short explanation:



Long:

We see that the sequence is (x-#n letter of alphabet) all the way to z. Eventually, one binomial will end up as $(x-x)$. By the reflexive property, $x=x$. We subtract $x$ from both sides, giving us: $x-x=0$. By the Zero Multiplicative Property, anything multiplied by 0 is 0. Therefore, the numerator equals 0. 0 divided by anything is still zero, so we get our desired solution: $\boxed{0}$.



Short:

Eventually, in the finite sequence, there will be $(x-x)$, which equals 0. Anything multiplied by 0 is 0, and as long as the numerator is 0, the answer is 0. Therefore, the solution is $\boxed{0}$.

topics.text:
NOTE: Use google translator to translate from Italian to English



We must state that:

$- (- x) = x$



Let's start with

$- (-x)$

$= - (-x) + 0$ (since $x + 0 = x$)

$= - (- x) + (- x) + x$ (because $x = -x + 0$)

$= (- (- x) + (- x)) + x$ (I apply the associative property of addition to the first two addends)

$= 0 + x$ (because $ -x + x = 0$, in this case $x = -x$ and $-x = -(-x)$)

$= x$ (because $x + 0 = x$)

topics.text:
A person named George had a strange habit that on the $n$th day of any month, he spends $n$ dollars. For example, on the $23$rd, he spends $23$ dollars. On five consecutive days, George found out that he spent $63$ dollars in a period of five days.

topics.text:
Emma goes to the store to buy apples and peaches. She buys five of each, hands the shopkeeper one

5 bill, but then has to give the shopkeeper another; she gets back some change. Jonah goes to the same store,

give the shopkeeper another 10 bill, and also gets some change. Finally, Helen goes to the same store to buy

in cents, that Helen can expect to pay.
